whoIsThisFor.heading: Who should take the JavaScript Developer I exam?

personas.label: Web developers moving to Salesforce
personas.description: You know JavaScript and want to learn how Lightning Web Components, Apex calls, and Salesforce security fit together.

personas.label: Salesforce developers learning JavaScript
personas.description: You build with Apex and LWC and want to strengthen your knowledge of JavaScript language behavior.

personas.label: LWC developers
personas.description: You create Lightning components and want a structured review of component lifecycle, events, asynchronous code, and browser standards.

examDifficulty.heading: How challenging is the JavaScript Developer I exam?
examDifficulty.summary: The exam focuses on JavaScript fundamentals as well as Salesforce component development. Be ready to read code and reason about scope, closures, prototypes, promises, and execution order, then apply those ideas to Lightning Web Components.
bullets: 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
65% to pass, which is 39 correct answers out of 60.
Execution order matters: Know how synchronous code, promise callbacks, and timers run.
LWC concepts matter: Review lifecycle hooks, wire versus imperative Apex, events, and component security.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Use a JavaScript console to predict a snippet’s output before running it. Practice closures, function binding, promises, and timers. Also build an LWC that reads data with wire and performs an imperative action from a user event.

examFormat.heading: JavaScript Developer I exam format
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or at a test center. It covers JavaScript language behavior and Salesforce development concepts.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Some questions ask you to predict what a code snippet returns, logs, or throws. Others ask which decorator, lifecycle hook, event pattern, or asynchronous approach fits a requirement.
bestWayToPass: Write and run small examples: Predict the result first, then use the browser console to check your understanding.
Understand the event loop: Separate synchronous work, promise microtasks, and timer tasks when tracing output.
Practice function context: Compare method calls, standalone functions, arrow functions, and callbacks.
Build an LWC that uses Apex: Read data with wire and call Apex imperatively when an action needs explicit timing.

certificationCard.description: Covers JavaScript fundamentals and Lightning Web Components, including ES6 syntax, scope, closures, prototypes, promises, async/await, the event loop, component lifecycle, Apex calls, and Lightning Web Security. The exam is 60 scored questions in 105 minutes, with a 65% pass mark, weighted towards Objects, Functions, and Classes (25%) and Variables, Types, and Collections (23%).

blocks.heading: Scope, Closures, and this
blocks.body: A closure is a function together with access to variables in the scope where it was created. It can preserve values after the outer function returns. In loops, var shares one function-scoped binding; let creates a new block-scoped binding for each iteration. The value of this depends on how a function is called. A method call uses the object before the dot, while a standalone strict-mode function has undefined as this. Arrow functions do not create their own this; they use the surrounding value.

blocks.heading: Prototypes and Classes
blocks.body: JavaScript looks up properties on an object and then along its prototype chain. Class syntax provides a familiar way to create constructor functions and prototype methods. Methods declared in a class body are placed on the class prototype; fields assigned on each instance belong to that instance. extends sets up inheritance, and super refers to the parent class. instanceof checks whether a constructor’s prototype appears in an object’s prototype chain.

blocks.heading: Promises and Error Handling
blocks.body: A promise represents a result that may become available later. It settles once, either fulfilled or rejected. then, catch, and finally register handlers, and each then creates a new promise for the next step. Returning a value passes it down the chain; returning a promise makes the chain wait for it. An async function always returns a promise, and await pauses that function until the promise settles. Promise.all rejects if an input rejects, Promise.allSettled reports every result, and Promise.race settles with the first input to settle.

blocks.heading: The Event Loop
blocks.body: JavaScript runs synchronous code on the call stack. After that work completes, the runtime processes queued promise callbacks (microtasks) before taking the next timer or other task. A setTimeout callback therefore runs after synchronous code and queued promise callbacks, even when its delay is zero. Long synchronous work blocks the event loop and delays user interface updates.

blocks.heading: Lightning Web Components, Apex, and Security
blocks.body: LWC uses web component standards, including a component’s own shadow tree. The constructor runs before the element is connected. connectedCallback runs when it is inserted into the DOM; renderedCallback runs after rendering and may run more than once; disconnectedCallback is used for cleanup. The wire service provisions data reactively when its parameters change. Imperative Apex calls give JavaScript explicit control over when a request is made. Custom events communicate with parent components; event options determine whether an event crosses a shadow boundary. Lightning Web Security limits access to resources outside a component’s permitted scope.

scenarioTips.h2: How to prepare for the JavaScript Developer I exam
scenarioTips.intro: For code questions, trace the execution and state before choosing an answer. For LWC questions, identify the component lifecycle moment or data access pattern involved.

blocks.heading: Predict, Then Run
blocks.body: Write a short example, predict its output, and then run it. This helps with scope, closures, function context, and execution order.

blocks.heading: Trace the Event Loop
blocks.body: Run synchronous code first, then promise callbacks, then timer callbacks. Use that order when tracing promise and setTimeout examples.

blocks.heading: Check this in Context
blocks.body: Compare a method call, standalone function, arrow function, and method passed as a callback. The call style determines the value of this.

blocks.heading: Select Promise Methods by Behavior
blocks.body: Promise.all rejects when an input rejects; allSettled reports each outcome; race settles with the first promise to settle.

blocks.heading: Match Lifecycle Hooks to Timing
blocks.body: Use connectedCallback for setup that does not need rendered markup, renderedCallback for work after rendering with a guard against repeats, and disconnectedCallback for cleanup.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Related credentials for JavaScript developers
nextCertsAfter.intro: Build on JavaScript and LWC skills with a Salesforce developer or platform credential.

sampleQuestions.question: Which JavaScript feature provides a standard way to work with asynchronous results without blocking the main thread?
options: Synchronous loops run on the main thread
Promises and async/await handle asynchronous results
Callbacks are the only way to handle asynchronous code
sampleQuestions.explanation: Promises and async/await let code handle results that arrive later while the main thread continues other work.
whyWrong: A synchronous loop can block the main thread while it runs.
Variable declarations define bindings but do not manage asynchronous results.
Callbacks can handle asynchronous work; promises and async/await are also standard options.

sampleQuestions.question: What are Lightning Web Components used for in Salesforce?
options: Creating Salesforce email templates for customers
Building interactive UI components on the Lightning Platform
Running Apex exclusively on the server
sampleQuestions.explanation: LWC is Salesforce’s component model for building interactive user interfaces on the Lightning Platform.
whyWrong: Email templates are not LWC user interface components.
Data modeling defines stored records rather than reactive UI components.
LWC builds interactive components for the Lightning Platform.

sampleQuestions.question: Which keyword declares a block-scoped variable in JavaScript?
sampleQuestions.explanation: let creates a binding scoped to the nearest block.
whyWrong: let, not function, declares a block-scoped variable.
var is function-scoped rather than block-scoped.
global is not a JavaScript declaration keyword.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the shadow DOM provide for a web component?
options: Storing API keys in a browser component
Rendering the component on the server
sampleQuestions.explanation: The shadow DOM provides an encapsulated component tree for markup and styles.
whyWrong: The shadow DOM encapsulates a component’s tree and styles.
Database queries are performed through data services, not the shadow DOM.
Secrets should not be stored in client-side components.

sampleQuestions.question: Which LWC decorator exposes a public component property to its parent?
sampleQuestions.explanation: The @api decorator marks a property or method as part of the component’s public interface.
whyWrong: @api exposes a property or method publicly.
@invocable is not the LWC public-property decorator.
@track is not the decorator for exposing a property to a parent.

sampleQuestions.question: Which wire adapter retrieves a record by its record ID?
sampleQuestions.explanation: getRecord retrieves a Salesforce record when supplied with its record ID and requested fields.
whyWrong: getListUi is not the record-by-ID adapter.
getObjectInfo returns metadata rather than a record.
createRecord creates records rather than retrieving one by ID.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the JavaScript spread operator do?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Spread syntax expands iterable values and can copy or merge object properties.
whyWrong: Class declarations use class syntax.
Error handling uses try/catch or rejection handlers.
Spread syntax expands iterable values and can copy or merge object properties.

sampleQuestions.question: Which LWC lifecycle hook runs when a component is added to the DOM?
sampleQuestions.explanation: connectedCallback runs when the component is inserted into the DOM.
whyWrong: renderedCallback runs after rendering.
connectedCallback runs when the component is inserted into the DOM.
disconnectedCallback runs when the component is removed.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the @wire service do in LWC?
options: Supplies data reactively when parameters change
Exposes a property to parent components
sampleQuestions.explanation: @wire provisions data reactively from a supported adapter or Apex method when its configuration changes.
whyWrong: @wire is not a general automatic state tracker.
@wire provisions data reactively when its configuration changes.
Event handlers respond to events; they do not provide wire data.

sampleQuestions.question: Which array method returns a new array by transforming each element?
sampleQuestions.explanation: map calls a function for each element and returns a new array of the results.
whyWrong: push modifies an array by adding an element.
map returns a new array of transformed values.
splice changes the original array.

sampleQuestions.question: In a DOM event handler, what does event.target identify?
options: The global window object in the browser
sampleQuestions.explanation: event.target identifies the element that dispatched the event.
whyWrong: event.target identifies the element that dispatched the event.
window is a global browser object, not necessarily the event source.
document represents the page document, not necessarily the event source.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Aura concept is closest to an LWC public property marked with @api?
sampleQuestions.explanation: A public Aura attribute exposes a value on the component in a way that is similar to an LWC public property.
whyWrong: aura:method exposes a method, not an attribute.
A publicly accessible aura:attribute is similar to an LWC public property.
aura:registerEvent declares an event, not a public attribute.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a JavaScript module?
sampleQuestions.explanation: A module groups code in a file, can export bindings for reuse, and has its own scope.
whyWrong: A module can contain variables but is more than a declaration.
A module can include a class but is not limited to one.
A module can contain many functions and is not just one function.

sampleQuestions.question: Which API is used for programmatic navigation in LWC?
sampleQuestions.explanation: NavigationMixin.Navigate is the supported LWC pattern for navigating to a page reference.
whyWrong: history.push is not the standard LWC navigation pattern.
LWC provides NavigationMixin for programmatic navigation.
window.location can navigate, but it is not the recommended LWC navigation API.

sampleQuestions.question: What does const prevent in JavaScript?
sampleQuestions.explanation: const prevents reassignment of the binding, but an object stored in it may still be mutable.
whyWrong: const declarations are block-scoped.
const declares a variable binding.
Objects assigned to const can still be mutated.
